one_line_purpose: Real-time audio quality assessment for voice apps.
problem_solved: Determining if an audio recording is clean enough to process by analyzing acoustic metrics.
architecture_summary: The system processes audio by loading files or streaming chunks from a microphone. Audio is divided into overlapping frames. For each frame, it computes acoustic metrics: RMS, spectral flatness, spectral concentration, SNR, and noise floor. These per-frame metrics feed into a `RollingStats` object that maintains historical buffers for noise floor and RMS values, enabling the calculation of temporal variance and aggregated background dBA. Finally, an `assess_quality` function uses these aggregated metrics in an SNR-gated tiered assessment logic to determine a quality tier (excellent, good, fair, or poor) and a descriptive reason. For real-time streaming, a `LiveDetector` adds a hysteresis buffer to stabilize tier changes.
key_features: Real-time audio quality assessment for voice applications
Analyzes audio using four acoustic metrics: SNR, Spectral Flatness, Temporal Variance, Background dBA
Provides numerical values for all assessed metrics and a reason for the tier decision
Supports real-time streaming analysis from a microphone (`LiveDetector`) with tier change callbacks
Command-line interface (CLI) for file assessment and live listening
Auto-calibration for microphone input to account for hardware and OS processing differences
Benchmarks against a reproducible test set mixed from VocalSet and MUSAN datasets
Stabilizes streaming assessment with a hysteresis buffer (new tier must persist for N frames)
Estimates noise floor using 10th percentile of recent RMS values
Reports room loudness as the median of recent RMS values
Includes a `spectral_concentration` metric to gauge how tonal vs. broadband an audio frame is
notable_code_decisions: SNR-gated tiered assessment: high SNR allows for louder background noise without penalty, while low SNR triggers a composite score from all four metrics.
Hysteresis buffer for streaming (3-frame stability) to prevent flickering of quality tiers.
Noise floor estimation using the 75th percentile of the power spectrum (after filtering silent bins) and 10th percentile of recent RMS values for background dBA.
Background dBA calculation uses the median of recent RMS values to track sustained noise and ignore transient silences.
Uses `scipy.signal.resample_poly` for high-quality audio resampling during file loading.
The `spectral_concentration` metric was introduced to gate SNR fast-paths, preventing noise-like audio with a high spectral SNR from being incorrectly classified as 'excellent'.
Modular design separating IO, metrics, rolling state, assessment logic, CLI, and live detection into distinct modules.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: Calibrated for voice/recording quality (clean enough to process), not subjective pleasingness.
Background dBA is a calibrated proxy, not a certified acoustic dB meter (does not use IEC 61672 A-weighted filter).
Requires calibration (`voicequal listen --calibrate`) once per new machine or microphone setup due to varying signal levels.
Assumes reasonable audio input; no built-in echo cancellation or noise suppression.
Accuracy can vary if the OS pre-processes mic audio (e.g., macOS Voice Isolation, browser noise suppression), even with calibration.

Known weakness in `v0.1.1`: low exact accuracy (5.0%) for `very_loud_snr` category (voice mixed with noise at ~5 dB SNR) because spectral SNR can read high for loud vocals buried in noise. `v0.2.0` plans to address this with Voice Activity Detection (VAD) gating for RMS-domain SNR estimation.
what_it_demonstrates: The project demonstrates a practical application of digital signal processing (DSP) for real-time audio analysis, including: feature extraction (RMS, SNR, spectral flatness, spectral concentration), rolling statistics for temporal context, custom rule-based classification logic, and stream processing with hysteresis. It showcases how to build a usable Python library with a CLI, benchmarks, and clear API for both file-based and live streaming audio data.
